role.altitude: The food science technician keeps preparing samples, looking down the microscope, running tests, showing new staff the methods and coaching the team; moving microscope images by hand, collecting paper sign-off sheets, taking requests by mail and scanning records for gaps shrink.
skills_to_grow: Running training matrices in the quality system
role.ambitious_version: A technician whose bench time goes to the samples, not to paper.

tasks.short: Prepare slides, examine chemical or biological samples under a microscope to identify cell structures, bacteria or extraneous material, capture images, and record findings.

steps.what: Technician prepares slides and samples
Technician examines the samples under the microscope to identify cell structures, bacteria or extraneous material
Technician photographs findings and moves the images to the sample record
Technician records the findings

tasks.design: The microscope camera saves images straight to the sample's record in the laboratory system, named by the sample barcode, instead of the technician transferring and renaming files. Preparing slides and examining samples stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Images were moved and renamed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Microscope cameras linked to the laboratory system.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a hair fragment from a plant fibre.

reach.learn: Whether images are found with the sample.

evidence.claim: A laboratory information system barcodes samples, assigns tests and logs each change.

assumptions: Boundary: microscopic examination; recording and compiling test results (task 7579) is a sibling task.
s4 is part of recording test results, which sibling task 7579 covers; its saving is counted there.
Preparing and examining keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of microscopes with connected cameras.
research_questions: Are images linked to every sample?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older microscopes without a linked camera, so images are still moved and renamed by hand (s3 keeps 90) (1.0); high: cameras save to the sample record (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan training for newly hired laboratory personnel, demonstrate methods, assign SOPs and track read sign-offs, observe and assess competence, and record the competence sign-off.

steps.what: Technician plans the training programme for newly hired laboratory personnel
Technician demonstrates methods at the bench
New hire reads each assigned SOP and signs it as read and understood in the quality system
Technician assigns SOPs to read and collects paper read-and-understood sign-offs
Technician observes trainees performing tests and assesses competence
Technician records the competence sign-off in the training record: on paper today, in the quality system after the change

tasks.design: A training matrix in the quality system lists the SOPs and competences each lab role needs, so the plan for a new hire is generated per role. The system assigns SOPs and records electronic read sign-offs, instead of paper sheets collected and filed. The technician writes each competence sign-off in the training record in the quality system; this first record keeps its time. Demonstrating methods and assessing competence stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training plans and sign-offs were kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Training matrices and electronic sign-offs in quality systems.
tasks.still_hard: Methods learned only by doing many times.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a trainee's pipetting habit that will skew results.

reach.learn: Whether training records are complete at audit.

evidence.claim: Official control labs must be accredited to the testing standard, which requires validated software.

assumptions: Boundary: training new laboratory staff; supervising technicians (task 22261) is a sibling task.
s3 saves collecting and filing paper sign-off sheets; the new hire signs electronically (s2b, share 1, other role). s5 is the first record of the competence decision and keeps its full time.
Demonstrating and assessing keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of new hires per year.
research_questions: Are new staff signed off sooner?

incremental.description: Technician keeps the training matrix current with SOP changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few hires in roles the training matrix does not yet cover (s1 keeps 80), and SOPs partly still on paper (s3 keeps 70) (6.9); high: many hires and SOPs in the matrix (14.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive requests and samples, plan the day's tests, prepare test batches, run tests, record results, and discuss them to provide assistance to food scientists in research and development, production technology or quality control.

steps.what: Scientist submits the test request in the laboratory system
Technician receives samples and checks them against the requests: requests by mail and hand labels today, registered requests with printed labels after the change
Technician plans the day's tests from open requests
Technician prepares test batches for research and development, production technology or quality control
Technician runs the tests
Technician records the results
Technician discusses results with the scientist

tasks.design: Scientists submit test requests in the laboratory system, which prints barcode labels and registers the samples, instead of the technician taking requests by mail and labelling by hand. A worklist per instrument shows open tests with due dates, so the day plan is a view, not a handwritten list. Preparing batches, running tests and discussing results stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by mail and the day was planned on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Request forms and worklists in laboratory systems.
tasks.still_hard: Ad hoc requests made at the bench.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a scientist really needs the result before lunch.

evidence.claim: A laboratory information system barcodes samples, assigns tests and logs each change.

assumptions: Boundary: assisting scientists; recording and compiling results (task 7579) and computing product factors (task 7578) are sibling tasks.
s5 is part of recording test results, which sibling task 7579 covers; its saving is counted there.

Preparing, testing and discussing keep their full time. Scientists submit requests themselves (s0, share 1, other role), about the time a request mail took. s2 keeps 60 because ordering and batching the day stay with the technician; only compiling the list goes.
unknowns: Share of requests made at the bench.
research_questions: Do results arrive on time more often?

incremental.description: Technician registers bench requests in the system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly ad hoc bench requests that are not entered in the system (s1 and s2 keep 90) (1.7); high: mostly planned requests in the system (7.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review open tests and workload, assign work, scan records for gaps, review and approve results, coach technicians, and handle rosters to supervise other food science technicians.

steps.what: Supervisor reviews open tests and workload per technician and instrument
Supervisor assigns work to other science technicians
Supervisor scans records for missing or out-of-specification entries
Supervisor reviews and approves technicians' results
Supervisor coaches technicians and solves problems at the bench
Technician submits a leave request in the HR self-service tool
Supervisor handles rosters and leave

tasks.design: The laboratory system shows open tests by instrument and due date, so the supervisor sees the workload without collecting it from lists. Rules flag missing entries and results outside specification for review, instead of the supervisor scanning every record. Leave requests go through the HR self-service and roster tool. Assigning work, approving results and coaching stay with the supervisor. Per-person views are used to plan work, not to rate technicians.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workload and record gaps were found by going through lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Laboratory system worklists, review rules and roster tools.
tasks.still_hard: Problems that never show in the records.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a technician is overloaded before errors appear.

reach.learn: Whether workload is spread more evenly.

evidence.claim: Systems fit to monitor performance, such as per-user audit trails, need works council consent.
A laboratory information system generates certificates with e-signatures and audit trails.

assumptions: Boundary: supervising technicians; maintaining records of results (task 20394) and training new hires (task 20397) are sibling tasks.
The works council consents before workload views per technician are used.
Assigning, approving and coaching keep their full time. Team members submit leave in self-service (s5b, share 1, other role); s6 keeps 60 for deciding on leave and setting the roster.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small teams where the workload view and flags save little (s1 keeps 70, s3 keeps 60) (10.4); high: larger teams with many tests (16.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
